claims.claim: **Hypertrophy of the pyloric muscle causes gastric outlet obstruction.** It usually presents at **2–6 weeks** with **progressive non-bilious vomiting**, is unlikely after 12 weeks, and definitive treatment is **pyloromyotomy**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** male · first born · parental (especially maternal) history · preterm birth · younger maternal age · **postnatal macrolide exposure** · formula feeding · maternal smoking in pregnancy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vomiting is recurrent and increasingly forceful**, may be projectile, often shortly after feeds; the infant may seem hungry afterwards. Non-bilious; blood-stained in under 10%.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pyloric mass:** olive-shaped, in the right upper quadrant along the lateral border of rectus abdominis, **best felt from the left** with the infant settled and supine; may need repeated or prolonged examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early presentations lack the classic signs.** Visible peristalsis and a palpable mass are often absent and **are not required to consider the diagnosis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess the degree of dehydration, weigh, and plot against previous weights.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials:** UTI · gastroenteritis · GOR · surgical causes such as volvulus or malrotation · congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Capillary or venous gas for electrolytes and glucose.** Prolonged vomiting gives a **hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis**, proportionate to symptom duration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal ultrasound is 95% sensitive.** ⚠️ **Repeat it if suspicion persists** after an equivocal first scan.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Gain IV access, correct fluids, electrolytes and acid-base, stop oral feeds**; if vomiting stays profuse even with feeds stopped, pass a nasogastric tube.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delay surgery until dehydration, electrolytes and acid-base are corrected — above all, until serum bicarbonate is normal**, because metabolic alkalosis risks post-operative hypoventilation/apnoea.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resuscitation fluid: 0.9% sodium chloride**, only as required — not every infant needs it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Deficit: 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose** (volumes per the dehydration and IV fluid guidelines). ⚠️ **Add potassium when the infant is passing adequate urine (1–2 mL/kg/hr).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team whenever pyloric stenosis is suspected.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Confirmed or strongly suspected: transfer early to a paediatric surgical centre**, after an initial management plan has been put in place.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the ultrasound does not support pyloric stenosis, differentials have been considered, the infant is well and tolerating feeds, and follow-up is planned.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Pyloric stenosis' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Pyloric_stenosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
